In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the clinical, laboratory and radiographic characteristics of chronic recurrent multifocal (non-bacterial) osteomyelitis in children.

the following questions: What are the clinical features, laboratory and histological findings, and diagnostic and treatment strategies in children and adults diagnosed with CNO/CRMOS and SAPHO? How does the clinical course and outcome differ between the two age groups?

the question, whether the clinical picture, the diagnostic and therapeutic approach and the prognosis of chronic non-bacterial (bacterial) osteomyelitis are similar in children and adolescents and in adult patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNO/chronic multifocal non-bacterial osteitis (CMNBO) and SAPHO in children and adults may be the same disease.
CNO/chronic multifocal osteomyeltitis (CNO/CNO) is a rare inflammatory disorder, which can be diagnosed in both, pediatric as well as adult patients.
CNO/ CRMO and SAPH0 are the same disease in children and adults and that they need a similar diagnostic and treatment approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children and adults with CNO have similar clinical features but differ in the frequency of bone lesions and the use of diagnostic imaging techniques.
children with CNO/CRNO and adults with SAPHO have a similar clinical presentation and laboratory findings, and a similar outcome, and should therefore be treated in the same way.

the diagnosis of CRMO/CNO/SAPHO syndrome is similar in both children and adults and should be based on the clinical and laboratory findings and the exclusion of other differential diagnoses such as infections, malignancies or autoinflammatory diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children and adults with chronic non-bacteria osteomyelitis should be treated similarly, and that bisphosphonates are a good first line therapy for both age groups.

the diagnosis of CNO/CRNO and SAPHO should be considered in patients of all ages presenting with bone and/or skin lesions and that a prompt diagnosis is essential for an early treatment and a favorable outcome.
